name: tic-tac-toe
_: The whole token contract existed only as a drawing: the wireframes declare
about thirty tokens and src/global.css was two import lines, so the app
hand-wrote slate-*/sky-*/rose-* that happened to coincide because the
design had been drawn FROM slate. Nothing enforced the coincidence.
`brand` here is the interactive blue, which is what the ramp slot means
everywhere else. The near-black #111827 was never a brand ramp — it is the
splash colour and must stay in step with app.config.ts, so it is reserved.
This app has no ramp stops other than 500. That is allowed: only `-500` is
required, and lint check 10 catches any stop that gets used without being
declared. The drift page reports ramp completeness rather than forcing
seven invented hexes.
Corrections applied from core: radius 2xl 28px -> 24px (it was the only
app where rounded-2xl differed), h1 34px -> 36px, and the desktop phone
frame it never had.

shadows._: The board tile lift. Uses the shared tint so it follows the theme.

_: Rule 01: blue is X and rose is O. Nothing else on the board may be
either. The difficulty scale is a separate reserved axis — it was being
re-invented in GameModeCard as emerald-700/amber-700/rose-700, which is
three different hues for three concepts that already had tokens.
`icon` exists because lucide takes a colour prop, not a className. It is
the one place in this system where a JS value is the only option, which
is why tokens.ts is a generated output rather than a hand-kept mirror.

gradients._: Named brand-x/brand-o, NOT mark-x/mark-o: the mark tokens are the flat glyph colour and a gradient cannot share their name. The set already used --brand-x-from/--brand-x-to for exactly this.

_: How this set's old names become canonical ones. Consumed by
scripts/migrate-screens.mjs, which rewrites the wireframes and the app
source in one pass.
vars are CSS custom properties in style= and stylesheets; classes are
Tailwind token names in class= and className=.

__raw._: Raw Tailwind palette in the app source. The light side coincides with the design values because the set was drawn FROM slate; nothing enforced it, which is the point. The DARK side does not coincide — the app invented its own dark values while the wireframe's .phone--dark scope said something else. The wireframe is the spec, so these map onto the design's dark values and the dark theme shifts slightly. Prefix-qualified keys (bg:, border:, text:) exist because white/10 is a hairline on an edge and a raised surface on a fill.

styles._: Inline declarations that needed a decision rather than a translation. Each one is a stated choice; anything not listed is left in place and counted, so the leftover number stays honest.

_: Structural CSS this product needs and the canon cannot know about.
The board is a device, like the phone frame: a fixed 3x3 grid whose
geometry is copied from src/constants/styles.ts so the wireframe and the
app agree on gap, padding and border. Expressing it as utilities would
scatter six coupled numbers across every screen that draws a board.
This is a narrow exception to rule 5, declared per set and checked: the
lint allows exactly the classes named here and nothing else. The first
version of the shim had no such hook, silently dropped these two rules,
and the board rendered as a single column on every screen.
